claims.text: Shopify's official AI connectors hold one store at a time, even within one organization; switching starts a new authorization (Shopify staff, 7 Oct 2026; hosted MCP switch-shop description, probed 30 Oct 2026)

Practitioners who work across several stores voice the one-store limit in their own words: a theme developer with nine stores ('Parallel agents cannot work on different stores at all') and a consultant connecting a client's two regional stores to Claude Code

Multi-store AI access to Shopify is already offered by others: alex-brecher/shopify-multi-store (MIT, v2.0, 5 stars), Matrixify (several shops per assistant since June 2026), ShopMCP, Datadrew, SyncWith

Shopify service partners are an identifiable, reachable population (5,454 listed in the Partner Directory; 837 US tiered partners; 40,000 partners referred a merchant in 2025) but no source counts those working 5-30 live client stores with AI assistants
Merchants running several of their own stores mostly solve cross-store work with native Plus analytics, sync apps and spreadsheets; their voiced pain is catalog matching, not AI access
Store acquirers distrust seller screenshots, but live access needs the seller to grant it and no source shows buyers using AI assistants across several target stores
Running several Shopify CLI commands at once on one login logged a developer out (six parallel theme pulls); running them one at a time behind a lock was stable
Shopify points multi-store AI work to its own CLI (store auth per store, store execute --store) and tells merchants to use official integrations rather than build their own token-based ones

Whether multi-store AI access is still an unmet gap: Grok finds two gaps (remembered authorization inside chat apps; parallel-safe CLI use), Codex finds no marketwide gap given Matrixify, ShopMCP and community MCPs
